observation: C++ reproduces one eight-block allocation (16,484 bytes, mode 1), all 96 chunk queries (83 ready, 13 empty), and all 83 releases. Returns, allocation arguments, four globals and all 100 ring metadata bytes agree; all 21 original control artifacts remain exact.
interpretation: Concrete recovered ring methods now feed the field stream and wave callback source. The shared ring owner keeps expected sequence, selected allocation, separate active count and debugger selector explicit. Heap allocation, CD producers and audio internals remain named unresolved game dependencies.

reviewers: Codex /root independent source/probe/comparison review and sanitized rebuild

preconditions: Pinned development environment and qualified original resident profile.
Unchanged original route with a separately built uninstrumented control.
commands: nix --extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes' develop path:./nix --command ctest --preset sanitize -R '^disc-stream-reconstruction$'

validation.expected: Exact owned ring state, original return values, allocation mode and byte count; corrupted input/output rejects.
validation.actual: Independent sanitized rebuild passes all 180 observed recovered calls and seven corruption cases. Connected synthetic tests execute real ring-to-stream-to-wave source.
validation.tolerance: Exact metadata, returns and call arguments. Unused payload bytes are synthetic storage only; these functions do not read them. Heap result and initial allocation bytes remain actual callee inputs, not reconstructed heap behavior.
